title: casting rides a door
what: A ticket enters the corpus through a door that refuses a malformed one, instead of by a hand writing a JSON file that nothing checks.
why: The ticket corpus is what every voyage anchors to — a proof's claim, a crossing's gate, a chart's clain all resolve against a ticket file. And a ticket enters that corpus because I typed a JSON file correctly. Nothing refuses a missing field, a duplicate id, an unparseable workflow string, or a berth path that resolves to nothing. The lived symptom is already measured on the corpus it produced: 263 tickets, `author` on 6%, `owner` in ~42 different phrasings, `cast_by` holding two different meanings. That is what an ungated store looks like from the inside, and every voyage is leaning on it.
how: The IOU is stated at cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py:38 and has been standing there: '/sorted files a ticket by writing a file; nothing refuses the write.' MEASURED 2026-09-09, and stated at the width the instrument actually covers: no Python module in cairn/, skills/ or bin/ creates a ticket file. The creator is a HAND — CC's, following /sorted step 5 — 264 times. cairn/tools/base/transitions.py has a ticket write door (set_phase, built under 9e7867aa1056) but it writes the PHASE on an existing ticket and explicitly refuses a `ticket=` the world does not hold, so creation is out of its scope by design. Approach: (1) a `cast_ticket` door beside set_phase in the same module, taking the /sorted berth path and writing the ticket file from it — the berth already holds the judged packet, so the door composes an existing judged artifact rather than re-judging; (2) it refuses on the store charter's required fields, on a duplicate id, on a workflow string parse_workflow cannot read, and on an intent_berth or sorted_berth that does not resolve; (3) it journals the act, so 'who cast this and when' becomes a record rather than an inference; (4) /sorted step 5 stops saying 'write the file' and starts saying 'fire the door'. DO NOT retro-red the 264 existing tickets — watchme_spec.py:34 records that exact stone being paid for twice already ('A CHECK THAT RETRO-REDS EVERY OPEN BOAT IS A CHECK THAT GETS DISABLED'), so the door gates ENTRY and a separate sweep reports the backlog without failing anything.
traces_to: Law 4 — the rule that a ticket must be well-formed is real, is written down in the store charter, and is enforced by nothing but my care while typing; that is the definition of a tracked debt rather than a resting state. Law 6 — the tickets store has an owner and an owner gates writes, and today writes arrive ambiently. Law 8 — the corpus is what every voyage's proof is anchored to, and an unvalidated corpus is a peer being leaned on without ever having been proven.
falsifier: DONE when a ticket cannot enter CairnCommons/tickets/ except through the door; when a malformed cast is refused with every lack named in one pass; when the act is journaled; and when /sorted step 5 fires the door rather than describing a file write. HORIZON: the next 10 casts after PROVED — all 10 journaled, zero hand-written files. WRONG INTENT if the door lands and hand-written tickets continue beside it, which is the measured failure shape of the phase door it sits next to (built 2026-09-08, 13 records in four days, then no caller); a door with no callers is worse than no door, because it reads as physics from the outside while the writes go round it.
children: none, because the judge, the writer and the journal are one door over one store — and _write_ticket already exists at transitions.py:2163, so the byte-level write is composed rather than built. The backlog SWEEP is not a child either: it reports and never fails, so it cannot hold this ticket open.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-casting-door-has-callers) -> [PROVED]

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: tickets journaled through the door, tickets arriving unjournaled, and the distinct calendar days spanned
watchme.consumer: whoever casts the next ticket, and e71983e8d76c (author + via), which cannot be enforced at all until this door exists
watchme.enough: 10 consecutive casts journaled through the door with zero unjournaled arrivals, across at least 3 distinct calendar days. THE DAYS CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS COPIED FROM THE FAILURE NEXT DOOR: the phase door took 13 records in FOUR DAYS and then went silent forever, so a burst on one day is exactly the shape that must not clear this watch. It can also go back down — one unjournaled arrival re-opens it.
watchme.trigger: each ticket appearing in CairnCommons/tickets/ — the store's own growth is the trigger, so a hand-written file fires the watch by existing

gates_bound.check_type: proofs beside the code, run twice, sealed under the tester with isolation
a red at PROVEME kicks back to this ticket
a sweep counts tickets whose creation is not journaled; new entries after PROVED must be zero
gates_bound.gate: the door is the only path
gates_bound.why: the whole ticket is this sentence. A door beside a still-open side path is decoration, and the store next door proved the pattern (55dc1f3d799b) by making the door the ONLY path rather than the preferred one

in: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the new casting door, beside set_phase; _write_ticket at line 2163 is the byte-level writer and is composed, not rebuilt
skills/sorted/SKILL.md step 5 + skills/sorted/intention+why.json — 'file to CairnCommons' becomes 'fire the door'
CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json — the required-field set the door judges against
a backlog SWEEP that reports the 264 existing tickets and fails nothing
out: RETRO-REDDING THE 264. Hard bound, not a preference: watchme_spec.py:34 records this stone being paid for twice, most recently 2026-08-03 when a scrub retagged 50 cast tickets and the rule redded all 50. Its conclusion is in the file — 'A CHECK THAT RETRO-REDS EVERY OPEN BOAT IS A CHECK THAT GETS DISABLED.'
Extending set_phase to also create. Its refusal of a ticket the world does not hold is load-bearing — it stops a typo'd id from silently minting a ticket.
A git pre-commit hook on tickets/. Fires after the reasoning is gone, and cannot journal who cast it (one committer on the commons repo).
Reshaping `owner` or migrating authorship — that is e71983e8d76c, this ticket's child in effect, and it needs this door to be enforceable at all.

open_for_akien: One, and it is a spec choice so it waits for you rather than for evidence: should the casting door live in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py beside set_phase, or in a tickets-store module of its own? Beside set_phase is where the byte writer and the journaling already are, and it is what I have assumed. Against it: transitions.py is already the biggest file in the system and it is the WORKFLOW authority, while this is a STORE door — the two are different jobs sharing an address. My read is beside set_phase for this build, with the split as its own later question once both doors have callers, because splitting an unused door is rearranging.

measured_at_cast.iou_address: cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py:38 — 'CASTING HAS NO CHOKEPOINT. /sorted files a ticket by writing a file; nothing refuses the write.'
measured_at_cast.modules_that_create_a_ticket: 0 in cairn/, skills/, bin/ — the creator is a hand, CC's, via /sorted step 5
measured_at_cast.existing_ticket_door: set_phase (transitions.py:2181, PROVED under 9e7867aa1056) — writes the PHASE on an existing ticket; refuses a ticket= the world does not hold, so creation is out of scope by design
measured_at_cast.failure_shape_next_door: the phase door built 2026-09-08 took 13 records across 4 days, then had no caller at all

decisions.text: D1: cast_ticket lives in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py directly beside set_phase (the open_for_akien read stands: pre-approved by Akien 2026-09-17, everything cast is pre-approved through BUILDME/PROVEME); splitting a tickets-store module out is a later question once both doors have callers.

D2: cast_ticket(doc: dict, *, actor: str, tickets_dir: Path | None = None) -> Path. doc is the assembled ticket (hand fields plus the berth-derived ones). tickets_dir defaults to the live CairnCommons/tickets (the module's _TICKETS); a proof hands a scratch one. The door collects EVERY lack, then raises CastRefused (a subclass of IllegalTransition) naming all of them in one message; on refusal nothing is written and nothing is journaled. On pass it returns the written path tickets_dir/<id>-<slug>.json, slug derived from title: lowercase, every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] becomes one '-', leading/trailing '-' trimmed, capped at 80 chars.
decisions.step: unlisted: the door's signature and its refusal

decisions.text: D3: the required set is _CAST_REQUIRED in transitions.py: id, title, date, owner, owning_intention, intention, why, traces_to, how, falsifier, node_class, workflow_and_state, watchme, sorted_berth, intent_berth — the 15 keys the store template names that are present on at least 73 of the 77 tickets cast since 2026-09-01 (measured 2026-09-18 over 308 tickets). A key lacks when absent, None, or a blank/whitespace string (watchme may be a dict or the string 'none, because <X>'; falsifier may be a string or the template's dict). Nothing else in the template is required; extra keys are allowed.

D4: (a) any required lack (D3); (b) id not exactly 12 lowercase hex chars, or a file already standing under tickets_dir named <id>.json or <id>-*.json, or the target filename already existing; (c) workflow_and_state that parse_workflow raises MalformedWorkflow on — the parser's own text is carried in the lack; (d) sorted_berth that is not an existing file, or is a file whose JSON lacks skill == 'sorted', or whose answers.workflow != doc['workflow_and_state'], or whose answers.node_class != doc['node_class'] — the door composes the judged packet, so a cast that disagrees with its berth is refused; intent_berth that is not an existing file, unless it is the string 'none, because <X>' where reason_has_referent(X) holds (imported lazily from cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector, the way the BUILDME lanes already are at transitions.py:1379). Berth paths resolve as given (absolute, or relative to the cwd).

D5: the write rides cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + newline, verb='cast', why='cast_ticket: <id> <title> by <actor>'). That journal line — at, caller (cgroup class), sha_before 'absent', and the stack frame transitions.py:<n>:cast_ticket — IS the 'who cast this and when' record. Before writing, the door stamps doc['cast'] = today's ISO date only when the key is absent, and touches no other key; authorship fields (author, via) are e71983e8d76c's and are not written here.

D6: cairn/tools/base/cast.py holds sweep_casts(commons_root: Path) -> dict. It reads artifact.read_journal(commons_root) once and classifies every tickets/*.json (names starting with '_' skipped) by the FIRST journal entry for its relative path: through_the_door (sha_before == 'absent' and some stack frame ends with ':cast_ticket'), journaled_beside (a creation entry, sha_before 'absent', without that frame), pre_door (first entry's verb is 'genesis'), unjournaled (no entry at all). It returns {'counts': {class: n}, 'tickets': {class: [relative paths]}, 'landing': <at of the earliest through_the_door entry or None>} and never raises on the backlog. The same module is the CLI: python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cast <fields.json> --actor <who> fires cast_ticket and prints the path (exit 0) or the refusal (exit 1); python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cast --sweep [commons_root] prints the sweep as JSON and exits 0 always. bin/cmd/cast registers it as 'cairn cast'.

D7: cairn/tools/base/probes/the_casting_door_has_callers.py declares a module-level frozen PROBE (cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe) with trigger, carry and enough, to='harbor_master', body {'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}. It reads the commons root from the pulse context (context.get('roots', {}).get('commons'), else the live CairnCommons) and memoizes ONE sweep_casts per pulse via once(context, 'casts', ...). Arrivals = tickets whose first journal entry is a creation (sha_before 'absent') at or after the landing (the earliest cast_ticket entry, DERIVED never hard-coded), in journal order. enough: at least 10 arrivals stand, the last 10 are all through_the_door, those 10 span at least 3 distinct calendar days (at[:10]), and zero arrivals since the landing are journaled_beside or unjournaled — one such re-opens it (it goes back down). trigger: at least one arrival stands and enough is false. carry: the counts, the offending relative paths, the days spanned, and owning_ticket('23089d52d805'). Constants _ENOUGH_CASTS = 10, _ENOUGH_DAYS = 3 from the ticket's watchme. No thresholds= keyword: HEAD's probe.py carries no Threshold type (336a781018ba adds it and its migration will declare this probe's numbers when that ticket lands).

D8: skills/sorted/SKILL.md step 5 replaces 'write it with cairn artifact write ... --verb cast --from <file>' with: assemble the fields to <scratchpad>/ticket_fields.json (no id needed — the door mints one; sorted_berth = the berth the door just printed) and fire 'cairn cast <scratchpad>/ticket_fields.json --actor cc'; the door judges, mints the filename, journals, prints the path. skills/sorted/intention+why.json 'what' says 'survivors are cast through cast_ticket' in place of 'survivors file to CairnCommons' (written through cairn artifact write --verb charter, poking recompile_gate.sh in the same act). CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json gains one later line under notes_on_the_store (Law 7, the earlier line stands) saying the 15-field required set is enforced by cast_ticket since 23089d52d805, and cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py:38's IOU sentence gains the residue line that entry now has a chokepoint; the backlog is reported by the sweep and never redded.
decisions.step: unlisted: the skill and the charters

decisions.text: D9: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_cast_ticket.py, PROVES {'23089d52d805': {'all': 'test_the_door_the_sweep_and_the_watch_end_to_end'}} plus narrow teeth. Every tooth plants a scratch commons (tickets/ + a sorted berth file + an intent berth file) and points the artifact door at it with artifact.set_diagnostic_roots({'cairn': repo, 'CairnCommons': scratch}) restored in finally; binds cast_ticket/CastRefused/sweep_casts/PROBE at call time. Teeth: (1) a well-formed doc casts, the file lands at <id>-<slug>.json, the journal's entry has verb cast, sha_before absent and a cast_ticket frame; (2) a doc lacking three required keys, with a bad id, a malformed workflow and a berth that disagrees is refused with EVERY lack named in one message and nothing written; (3) a duplicate id is refused; (4) sweep_casts classifies a hand-dropped file as unjournaled, a genesis-first file as pre_door, an artifact.write-created file as journaled_beside, and a door-cast one as through_the_door; (5) the probe over a scratch commons: not enough at 9 casts, not enough at 10 casts on one day, enough at 10 casts across 3 days, back to not-enough when a hand-dropped file appears; (6) the composite. Run twice bare; sealed by the tester; hollow under --hollow 23089d52d805 --seal. The build is committed only after the BUILDME crossing.

D10: seven steps in order: (1) edit transitions.py — CastRefused, _CAST_REQUIRED, _slug, cast_ticket beside set_phase; (2) CREATE cairn/tools/base/cast.py (sweep_casts + CLI) and bin/cmd/cast; (3) CREATE the WATCHME probe; (4) CREATE the proof; (5) edit skills/sorted/SKILL.md step 5; (6) write the two charter lines through the door (sorted charter via --verb charter + recompile_gate.sh; tickets store charter via the door) and the watchme_spec.py residue line; (7) prove twice, seal, hollow, verdict.
